intent: Determine whether bright/dark features between high facets of a rough surface arise from geometry, coherent speckle, polarization, material/subsurface variation or sensor artifacts
physics_equation: I(x)=|sum_j A_j(x) exp(i phi_j(x))|^2 (schematic coherent detector model)
reference_scope: Research literature and a test protocol; no surface height map, camera image, original sample or laser sensor measurement in this wave

competing_models.mechanism: Exposure, vignetting, saturation, gamma, sensor noise or digital preprocessing
competing_models.predicts: Dark pattern or contrast changes with imaging pipeline, settings or camera independent of physical surface
competing_models.discriminating_test: Calibrated dark and flat-frame controls, locked exposure, comparison across cameras; preserve raw unprocessed frames

competing_models.mechanism: Occlusion and masking by upper surface facets of lower valleys, most visible at oblique illumination
competing_models.predicts: Shadow location correlates with measured surface height and illumination angle; reverses or moves with illumination azimuth
competing_models.discriminating_test: Known-geometry synthetic relief with opposite virtual illumination azimuth; match real measured topography only under independent safe optical protocol

competing_models.mechanism: Interference of coherent wavefront contributions from random surface height or multiple scattering paths
competing_models.predicts: Intensity pattern granularity and correlations change with optical path/coherence or observation geometry, even if the physical surface remains unchanged
competing_models.discriminating_test: Reproducible interference simulation first; authorized enclosed optical sample later, compare normalized coherence controls with geometry and camera held as constant as possible

competing_models.mechanism: Fresnel polarization response, facet orientations, depolarization and multiple scattering
competing_models.predicts: Parallel and crossed analyzer channels can show different intensity and polarization statistics with angle and material
competing_models.discriminating_test: Calibrated synthetic Stokes/analyzer data; eventual appropriately supervised controlled co/cross polarization acquisitions with normalized exposure

competing_models.mechanism: Coating, absorption, grain/chemical difference or buried defect
competing_models.predicts: Persistent contrast can follow composition or wavelength even when geometry or viewing direction changes
competing_models.discriminating_test: Reference material/known coating control and independent material metrology if available; do not infer defects from image alone

competing_models.mechanism: Difference not explained by the tested and explicitly scoped models
competing_models.predicts: Pre-registered residual survives controls and independent replication
competing_models.discriminating_test: Blind independent repeat with documented instrument, raw files, calibration and negative controls

proposed_protocol.expected: Model that ignores roughness produces smooth/known reference; random surface phase creates granular simulated intensity; no validation of real rough surface
Direction-dependent dark valleys in known simulated relief, not equivalent to destructive interference dark pixels
Coherent versus decorrelated phase ensemble produces different speckle statistics with same synthetic surface descriptor
Change simulated analyzer orientation or independently calibrated polarization channels; compare co-cross statistics without changing exposure
Known smooth and rough material controls, dark/flat frames and independent image acquisition bound artifacts
Pre-registered predictions and blind another operator; preserve PASS, FAIL and HELD including unexplained residuals
